findings.title: Settlement as a physical receptacle
findings.claim: Alongside the settlement's ordinary place sense, its gathered and possessed interior can be pictured as a receptacle holding a privileged class, with the class's breach disturbing that contained civic space.
findings.mechanism: Qaryatan carries the supplied vessel-or-hollow branch by analogy; fīhā provides an independent interior relation, mutrafīhā attaches the class to the settlement, and fasaqu names an action occurring within it.
findings.reader_payoff: The settlement's interior becomes perceptible as a bounded civic space whose contents and order are implicated in the breach.
findings.containment: The receptacle image supplements rather than replaces the settlement sense; it does not make qarya lexically mean a vessel or attribute the breach to every resident.

epistemic.reason: A supplied qarya branch, explicit interior and possession relations, and a distinct local breach support a contained analogy; the vessel image is not the clause's ordinary lexical meaning.
